<objective>
Give Google sign-in something to click.

The owner configured real Google OAuth credentials and reported: *"I've setted it up, but there's
no UI to log in with google"* (UAT test 12, G-01-12). `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` is present in
`.env.local` and is a well-formed client id, so the component is not rendering inertly — it is
rendering, and what it renders is a consent checkbox and nothing else.
`app/(auth)/components/GoogleOneTap.tsx` offers Google only as `google.accounts.id.prompt()`,
Google's floating One Tap prompt, gated behind ticking that box. There is no button anywhere.
`COPY.cta.continueWithGoogle` exists in the copy deck and is interpolated into the checkbox label
rather than rendered as a CTA. And the component is mounted on `/login` only, so `/signup` — where
a new owner would reach for it — offers no Google path at all.

The implementation matches its stated deliverable (01-02 D14: "Google One Tap is wired to Supabase
Auth with a hashed nonce and FedCM"). What UAT surfaces is that the deliverable chose
One-Tap-only, and One Tap is a *prompt*: the browser may suppress it for FedCM restrictions,
third-party sign-in settings, a too-many-dismissals cooldown, or an unregistered JavaScript origin —
and when it does, ticking the box produces no prompt, no error and no feedback.

**As a** restaurant owner who set Google up, **I want to** see a Google button and press it,
**so that** signing in with Google is something I can do rather than something that may or may not
happen to me.

Purpose: D-01 locks Google sign-in into phase-01 scope. The nonce handling, FedCM flag and
consent-before-session ordering in the shipped component are all CORRECT and this plan preserves
every one of them; what it adds is a control that does not depend on a prompt the browser is free
to withhold.

Output: an always-present Google control on both auth pages, a copy row for the pre-consent state,
and a guard that fails when an auth page offering sign-in forgets to mount it.
</objective>

<platform_facts>
Established this session against Google's Identity Services JavaScript API reference. An executor
must not re-derive these from memory — the FedCM item in particular inverts the obvious fix.

**`google.accounts.id.renderButton(parent, options)`** — renders a real, always-present Google
button into a DOM element. `options` is a `GsiButtonConfiguration`:
`type: "standard" | "icon"`, `theme: "outline" | "filled_blue" | "filled_black" | "outline_dark"`,
`size: "large" | "medium" | "small"`, `text: "signin_with" | "signup_with" | "continue_with" | "signin"`,
`shape: "rectangular" | "pill" | "circle" | "square"`, `logo_alignment: "left" | "center"`,
`width` (string, pixels, max 400), `locale`, `click_listener`, `state`.

`text: "continue_with"` renders "Continue with Google" — the same wording as the existing
`COPY.cta.continueWithGoogle` contract row.

The rendered button uses the SAME `initialize()` configuration as `prompt()` — same `client_id`,
same `nonce`, same `callback`. It therefore inherits the hashed-nonce binding rather than creating
a second, unbound path. This is why it is the correct fix and a hand-rolled button calling
`prompt()` is not: a hand-rolled button still depends on the prompt appearing.

**`google.accounts.id.prompt(momentListener)`** — the momentListener is optional and receives a
`PromptMomentNotification`. **Under FedCM (`use_fedcm_for_prompt: true`, which this component sets
and must keep) the following are NOT delivered:** `isDisplayMoment()`, `isDisplayed()`,
`isNotDisplayed()`, `getNotDisplayedReason()`. `isSkippedMoment()` and `getSkippedReason()` are
only partially supported (the `user_cancel` reason is not delivered). Only `isDismissedMoment()`,
`getDismissedReason()` and `getMomentType()` are fully supported, and display-moment notifications
are *intentionally delayed by up to a minute* when FedCM is enabled.

**Consequence, stated plainly:** G-01-12's `missing:` item 2 asks for "feedback when the prompt does
not display (One Tap exposes a dismissed/skipped-moment callback)". Under the FedCM configuration
this product uses, the not-displayed callback does not arrive. Building the feedback on it would
produce code that never runs, inside a closed ticket. The reliable answer to "the prompt did not
display" is a control that never needed the prompt — the rendered button. The moment listener is
still attached, but only for the notifications FedCM actually delivers.

**And note what this claim is NOT: load-bearing.** The fix does not depend on it. `renderButton`
draws a real button through the same `initialize()` configuration and consults no prompt-moment
notification at all, so the rendered control stands whether Google's delivery behaviour holds or
changes tomorrow. That is why the constraint is written into a greppable comment and reported in the
summary rather than frozen into a blocking suite gate — a third-party platform fact wired into the
build is a fact the product then has to keep being true, and this one does not have to be.
</platform_facts>

<threat_model>
ASVS enforcement level 1. Block on **high**.

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| browser → Google Identity Services | The ID token is minted here; the nonce binding is what ties it to this page load |
| browser → Supabase Auth (`signInWithIdToken`) | The token is exchanged for a session; Supabase verifies the signature and the nonce |
| browser → `ensureAccount` Server Action | POST-reachable independently of this component; consent evidence is written here |
| `.env` → client bundle | `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are public by construction |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01-15-01 | Spoofing | `GoogleOneTap` nonce binding | high | mitigate | The rendered button reuses the SAME `initialize()` configuration as the prompt, so it inherits the hashed-nonce binding rather than opening a second unbound path. Task 1's `<behavior>` asserts the value passed to `initialize` is the SHA-256 hex digest of the value later passed to `signInWithIdToken`, computed in the test rather than inferred from two variable names. A token captured from another site or an earlier prompt is validly signed but carries the wrong nonce and is refused. |
| T-01-15-02 | Tampering | post-sign-in destination | medium | mitigate | The destination stays the hardcoded `/venues`. No redirect target may be read from the query string, from `state`, or from the Google response — an open redirect on an auth callback is how a sign-in flow becomes a credential-relay. Asserted by the absence of any dynamic push target in the component. |
| T-01-15-03 | Repudiation | consent before session (D-21) | medium | mitigate | Sign-in remains un-initiable until the consent box is ticked, and `ensureAccount(TERMS_VERSION)` still runs before any navigation and before anything the session could write. The known residual — `ensureAccount` is POST-reachable, so the checkbox is UI ordering and not a control — stays recorded verbatim on `actions/auth.ts` and is explicitly NOT claimed closed by this plan. `tests/auth/google-consent.test.ts` continues to prove the structural half at the database layer. |
| T-01-15-04 | Information Disclosure | `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | low | accept | An OAuth client id is public by design and is already in the shipped client bundle; rendering a button does not change its trust level. The OAuth client SECRET stays in Supabase Auth and no code path under `app/` or `components/` reads it. Task 1 asserts the real value never enters a diff. |
| T-01-15-05 | Denial of Service | One Tap dismissal cooldown | low | accept | Repeated prompting drives Google's too-many-dismissals cooldown, which suppresses the prompt. The moment listener stops re-prompting after a dismissal, and the rendered button is unaffected by the cooldown — which is the structural reason this is acceptable rather than merely tolerated. |
| T-01-15-06 | Elevation of Privilege | a Google owner reaching venue data | high | mitigate | Unchanged by this plan: a Google session is an ordinary authenticated principal, `public.create_venue()` refuses without an `accounts` row, and RLS resolves membership through `private.get_venue_role()`. Adding a control does not add a principal type. |
| T-01-15-SC | Tampering | npm/pip/cargo installs | high | mitigate | This plan contains no package-manager install task; Google Identity Services arrives through the existing `next/script` tag, which is not a package-manager surface. The gate is `git diff --stat pnpm-lock.yaml` being empty, asserted in both tasks. |

**Schema gate:** this plan modifies no file under `supabase/migrations/`, so no `[BLOCKING]`
schema-push task applies.
</threat_model>
